accuracy.evidence: Every sum in the lab was recomputed by hand: take-away rounds 70 − 30 = 40, 80 − 50 = 30, 60 − 20 = 40; fact rounds 9 − 4 = 5 → 90 − 40 = 50, 8 − 3 = 5 → 80 − 30 = 50, 6 − 4 = 2 → 60 − 40 = 20; number-line rounds 90 − 60 = 30 (6 jumps), 70 − 40 = 30 (4 jumps), 100 − 30 = 70 (3 jumps); missing tens 80 − 50 = 30, 50 − 30 = 20, 90 − 50 = 40; children's sums 70 − 30, 60 − 20, 90 − 50. Parameterised items keep a > b at every corner so differences are positive multiples of 10, as CCSS 1.NBT.C.6 requires (range 10–90). Standard wording checked against CCSS 1.NBT.C.6.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented place-value slips for subtracting tens (NCETM Y1–Y2 ready-to-progress 1NPV/2AS: 'children treat 7 tens − 3 tens as 7 − 3 and drop the unit'): writing the ones fact as the answer (decoy 4 in step 1, Ali/Hana, p5, challenge tag tensdrop), adding instead of taking away (decoys 100/110/140, Cal/Dev, m5, tag added), taking away ones not tens (fact card 90 − 4 = 86, Ivy says 85, m6, tag onesonly), and confusing the size of the jump with the number of jumps (step 3 predict '60', m3, tag jumps).

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed (under 30% similar to every flagship lab). 607 10 More or 10 Less (flagtenjump) moves by a single ten, 465 A Ten Is Ten Ones (flagbundle) only builds a ten, and 578 A Hundred Is Ten Tens (flagtenten) composes a hundred; none takes several bundles away from a multiple of ten, links a ones fact to a tens fact, counts tens jumps on a 0–100 line or finds a missing number of tens.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners physically take bundles away and see 'n tens left' before choosing 40 vs 4 vs 100, so naming the tens left as a number is discovered, not told. The fact step makes them choose between a take-away fact, an addition fact and a ones fact, the number line makes each jump one ten (stopping early or late is explained in tens), and the missing-tens step reverses the operation. The children's answers turn the three slips into things to diagnose.

predictions.evidence: Five locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the task disproves: '4' for 70 − 30, '5' for 80 − 30 after 8 − 3 = 5, '60' jumps for 90 − 60, '3' for 50 − ? = 20, and 'Nothing, he is right' for Ali's 4. The done message reports the learner's prediction against the answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with tagged wrong answers: tensdrop (that is the small fact; put the 0 back), added (taking away makes the number smaller), onesonly (take away tens, not ones), jumps and jumpsleft (each jump is one ten; 6 jumps lands on 40), addfact (you need a take-away fact). Lab mistakes are named too, e.g. 'You jumped back 5 tens, that is 50. 60 is 6 tens: jump 1 more.' and '80 − 3 = 77 takes away 3 ones'.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability passed (kid under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Kid sentences are short and use the precise terms multiple of 10, tens, bundle, take away and number line. Canvas text is one short instruction per step, and buttons say exactly what they do (Take away one ten, Fact: 9 − 4 = 5, Answer: 40, Jump back 10, Stop here).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and explanation similarity under 12% to all lessons. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (multiples of 10 are tens; take away bundles; use a fact and keep the 0; jump back on a number line). The adult text gives the standard, the task order and the named slips.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light theme for every step before, during and after Show me (/workspace/shots/st-*). Bundles are about 60 × 110 px tap targets in two rows of five, the take-away tray and answer tiles span the width, number-line labels stay readable (labels raised to 11 px after the first pass) and feedback wraps inside the canvas. A finished fact step now shows the fact and answer instead of stale tiles.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, challenge shown, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button (Take away one ten, Put one ten back, Fact: …, Answer: …, Jump back 10, Stop here, Bea says 40), and the canvas aria-label states the sum, bundles left and taken, and the frog's position after each action.
